newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SINGH STRIKES TO LIFT INDIA'S HOPES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SINGH STRIKES TO LIFT INDIA'S HOPES.

text.p: Medium-pacer Robin Singh captured three for 13 in nine overs against Bangladesh on Thursday to boost India's hopes of reaching the Asia Cup final.
Singh was one of the main contributors to India's effective out-cricket as they restricted Bangladesh to 130 for eight off 43 overs.
A shower ended the Bangladesh innings with five of the stipulated 48 overs still remaining, the game having already been cut from 50 overs after overnight rain delayed the start.
India need to score 131 off 20 overs or less if they are to displace Pakistan from second spot in the standings to qualify for Saturday's final against Sri Lanka.

After Sachin Tendulkar won the toss and put Bangladesh in to bat, tight bowling and sharp fielding kept their overall run rate under three an over, which was essential to India's chances of improving on their tournament net run rate to qualify.
Only the in-form Athar Ali Khan (33) and Aminul Islam (30) made any significant contributions as leg-spinner Anil Kumble epitomised the economical bowling with one for 17 in 10 overs.
